usedStatements: Rotating anodes use a tungsten stem to reduce weight.
Rotating anodes allow higher tube currents by distributing heat over a larger area.
The heel effect is greater with a larger anode angle.
Detectors with high detective quantum efficiency require lower patient doses for a given image quality.
A high grid ratio improves scatter rejection but decreases patient dose.
The equivalent noise index NI is a measure used to set tube voltage modulation in CT.
Flying focal spot technology improves sampling and resolution in CT.
Third generation scanners use a rotate-rotate geometry with a parallel beam.
Water‑equivalent phantoms are used to calibrate CT numbers.
A high pitch always results in gaps in helical CT data leading to poorer image quality.
